# Load packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| code-summary: "Load packages"
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("amt", "lubridate",
              "terra", "sf",
              "beepr", "tictoc",
              "leaflet")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Import GPS tracking data

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- read_csv("data/pig_all_steps_20260707.csv")

# Convert timezone after import (resets to GMT)
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    t1_  = with_tz(t1_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"),
    t2_ = with_tz(t2_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"), 
    hour = hour(t1_) + minute(t1_)/60 + second(t1_)/3600,
    hour_round = hour(t1_),
    month = month(t1_),
    season = case_when(month %in% c(11,12, 1, 2, 3, 4) ~ "wet",
                       month %in% seq(5,10) ~ "dry")
    )

```

## Plot the pig data

```{r}

# plot the data spatially coloured by ID
pig_all_steps %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Use leaflet to plot the data

```{r}
#| label: leaflet-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# convert to an sf object (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112)
# and reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet
pig_all_steps_sf <- pig_all_steps %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

pal <- colorFactor(viridisLite::viridis(n_distinct(pig_all_steps_sf$name)),
                    domain = pig_all_steps_sf$name)

# addCircleMarkers() draws one SVG element per point, and there are ~246k of
# them, which locks up the browser (and the VS Code webview in particular).
# Thin the points for display and draw them with WebGL via leafgl instead.
pig_map_pts <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(seq(1, n(), by = 1)) %>% # every 10th fix per pig
  ungroup()

pig_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
  leafgl::addGlPoints(data = pig_map_pts,
                      fillColor = pal(pig_map_pts$name),
                      fillOpacity = 0.6,
                      radius = 4,
                      popup = paste0("ID: ", pig_map_pts$name,
                                     "<br>Time: ", pig_map_pts$t1_)) %>%
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal,
            values = pig_map_pts$name, title = "Pig ID")

# The VS Code htmlwidget viewer struggles with large maps, so when working
# interactively write the map out and open it in the system browser. When the
# document is rendered, the widget is printed inline as usual.
if (interactive()) {
  map_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "pig_map.html")
  # selfcontained = FALSE writes a sibling _files/ folder, which avoids needing
  # pandoc on the path and is much faster to write for a map this size
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(pig_map, map_file, selfcontained = FALSE)
  utils::browseURL(map_file)
} else {
  pig_map
}

```

## Create a bounding box around the pig data to crop the other layers by

```{r}

pig_all_steps_sf

pig_aoi <- st_bbox(pig_all_steps_sf) %>% 
  st_as_sfc() %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 3112) %>% 
  st_buffer(dist = 2500) %>%
  st_bbox() %>% # the buffer creates curved corners so we need to get the bounding box of the buffered area
  st_as_sfc()

```

## Gamma - discrete periods

We will, fairly arbitrarily, split the day into 4 periods: dawn (4-8), day (8-16), dusk (16-20), night (20-4).

Note that the hour_round is the floor (from lubridate::hour), i.e. 4:50am is 4, is it is within the 4th hour.

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    day_period = case_when(hour_round %in% c(4,5,6,7) ~ "dawn",
                       hour_round %in% seq(8,15) ~ "day",
                       hour_round %in% seq(16,19) ~ "dusk",
                       hour_round %in% c(20,21,22,23,0,1,2,3) ~ "night")
  )
```

### How many landcover types are there?

```{r}

unique(landcover_cropped$Veg_class)
length(unique(landcover_cropped$Veg_class))

```

### Create landcover raster layers for each landcover type

One binary (0/1) layer per vegetation class, on the same grid as the Sentinel-2
exports so that all of the covariates stack without any resampling.

```{r}
#| label: landcover-dummy

# Use the ndvi layer as the template grid (20 m, EPSG:3112) so the
# landcover layers line up cell-for-cell with the remotely sensed covariates
lc_template <- deepcopy(ndvi)
lc_template[] <- NA # keep the geometry, drop the values

# Rasterise the polygons; a character field gives a categorical raster, where
# the levels table maps the integer cell values back to the class names
landcover_rast <- rasterize(vect(landcover_cropped), lc_template,
                            field = "Veg_class")
plot(landcover_rast)
lc_levels <- levels(landcover_rast)[[1]]

```

### What frequency do they occur in the data?

```{r}

landcover_vals <- terra::extract(landcover_rast, matrix(c(pig_all_steps$x2_, pig_all_steps$y2_), ncol = 2))
pig_all_steps_covs <- bind_cols(pig_all_steps, landcover_vals) 

pig_all_steps_covs %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(y = Veg_class, fill = Veg_class)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

### Recode based on their frequency in the data

```{r}

recode_df <- data.frame(
  
  old = c("Wet Rainforest Springfed", 
          "Water", 
          "Mudflat",
          "Melaleuca Woodland", 
          "Melaleuca Open Woodland",
          "Melaleuca Open Forest", 
          "Melaleuca Closed Forest",
          "Mangrove", 
          "Grassland",
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Eucalypt Woodland", 
          "Eucalypt Open Woodland",
          "Eucalypt Open Forest", 
          "Eucalypt Closed Forest",
          "Dry Rainforest"),
  
  new = c("Dry Rainforest", 
          "Water", 
          "Mudflat",
          "Melaleuca Woodland", 
          "Melaleuca Woodland",
          "Melaleuca Open Forest", 
          "Melaleuca Closed Forest",
          "Mangrove", 
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Floodplain Sedgeland",
          "Eucalypt Woodland", 
          "Eucalypt Woodland",
          "Eucalypt Open Forest", 
          "Eucalypt Open Forest",
          "Dry Rainforest")
)

```

### Apply recode to raster

```{r}

lvls <- levels(landcover_rast)[[1]]                 # data.frame: ID, Veg_class

# left join: recode_df only covers classes seen at pig locations, but the
# raster covers the whole study area, so classes absent from recode_df$old
# would otherwise be dropped (and turn into NA) rather than passed through
lvls <- merge(lvls, recode_df, by.x = "Veg_class", by.y = "old",
              all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

lvls$new[is.na(lvls$new)] <- lvls$Veg_class[is.na(lvls$new)]

landcover_rast_merged <- deepcopy(landcover_rast)
levels(landcover_rast_merged) <- data.frame(ID = lvls$ID, Veg_class = lvls$new)
landcover_rast_merged <- droplevels(landcover_rast_merged)  # collapses duplicate labels into shared levels

freq(landcover_rast_merged)   # check the merge worked as expected
plot(landcover_rast_merged)

```

### Create dummy variables for each landcover type

```{r}

# segregate() expands the categorical raster into one 0/1 layer per class
landcover_dummy <- segregate(landcover_rast_merged, other = 0)

# segregate() names the layers by the integer category ID, so map them back to
# the class names, as snake_case so they work as covariate names downstream
names(landcover_dummy) <- lc_levels$Veg_class[
  match(as.integer(names(landcover_dummy)), lc_levels$ID)] %>%
  str_to_lower() %>%
  str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]+", "_") %>%
  paste0("veg_", .)

landcover_dummy

# maxnl defaults to 16, so set it explicitly or the last few classes are dropped
plot(landcover_dummy, col = c("grey90", "darkgreen"), legend = FALSE,
     maxnl = nlyr(landcover_dummy), axes = FALSE,
     mar = c(1.5, 1.5, 2, 1.5))

```

### Write the landcover variables to file

```{r}

# write out as a single multi-layer GeoTIFF; INT1U + DEFLATE keeps it small
writeRaster(landcover_dummy, "mapping/landcover_dummy_20m.tif",
            overwrite = TRUE,
            datatype = "INT1U",
            gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "PREDICTOR=2"))

```

# Extract landcover values at the pig locations

```{r}

covariate_vals <- terra::extract(
  c(ndvi,
    ndwi,
    ndmi,
    landcover_rast_merged,
    landcover_dummy), 
  matrix(c(pig_all_steps$x2_, pig_all_steps$y2_), ncol = 2))
  
pig_all_steps_covs <- bind_cols(pig_all_steps, covariate_vals) 

# write to file
write_csv(pig_all_steps_covs, "data/pig_all_steps_covs_20260813.csv")

```

```{r}
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


# Subset tracking and environmental data

Given there are two clusters in the data, subset to the one that has most of the data, greatly reducing the total area needed for the spatial layers. This is particularly helpful for the AlphaEarth embeddings, which are ~4GB for the full extent.

## Subset tracking data

### Plot all of the data

```{r}

# plot the data spatially coloured by ID

  ggplot(aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

```{r}

  pig_all_steps_covs %>%
```

### Create bounding box

```{r}

pig_all_steps_covs_subset_sf <- pig_all_steps_covs_subset %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112)

pig_subset_aoi <- st_bbox(pig_all_steps_covs_subset_sf) %>% 
  st_as_sfc() %>% 
  st_buffer(dist = 2500) %>%
  st_bbox() %>% # the buffer creates curved corners so we need to get the bounding box of the buffered area
  st_as_sfc()

# plot the data with the bounding box
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = pig_subset_aoi) +
  geom_point(data = pig_all_steps_covs,
             aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = name),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  coord_sf() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Subset environmental covariates

### AlphaEarth embeddings

```{r}

# load and plot
alphaearth_embeddings <- rast("mapping/feral_pig_aoi_alphaearth_2025.tif")
plot(alphaearth_embeddings)

# crop by the bounding box
alphaearth_embeddings_crop <- crop(alphaearth_embeddings, pig_subset_aoi)
plot(alphaearth_embeddings_crop)

# save the cropped embeddings
writeRaster(alphaearth_embeddings_crop, "mapping/feral_pig_aoi_alphaearth_2025_crop.tif", overwrite = TRUE)

```
